overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of what a model needs from a prompt in order to do a task well. You'll be asked about what a model needs to be told, supplying context, using examples, and iterating on a prompt.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A manager types "Write a summary of the attached report" and gets a summary that is accurate and of no help for the decision her team has to make. Which element was most clearly missing from her prompt?

options.html: An output format, since the summary came back as plain paragraphs
options.text: An output format, since the summary came back as plain paragraphs
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Nothing in the scenario says the form of the summary was the problem. The summary didn't serve its purpose, which points to a missing goal: what the result is for.

options.html: A goal, since the model wasn't told what the summary was for
options.text: A goal, since the model wasn't told what the summary was for
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The goal is what the result is for. A summary written to support a decision differs from one written for the record, and the model had no way to know which was wanted.

options.html: An example, since the model had no sample summary to copy from
options.text: An example, since the model had no sample summary to copy from
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. An example mainly shows tone, length, and structure. The summary failed to serve its purpose, which points to a missing goal: what the result is for.

options.html: A constraint, since no word limit was set for the summary
options.text: A constraint, since no word limit was set for the summary
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A constraint sets a limit such as length or tone. The summary's fault was that it didn't serve its purpose, which points to a missing goal: what the result is for.

forms.stemHtml: Why does an instruction tend to work better when you include the reason for it?

options.html: The reason makes the prompt longer, and longer prompts get more care
options.text: The reason makes the prompt longer, and longer prompts get more care
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Length isn't the aim. A reason helps because it lets the model apply the instruction to cases the instruction didn't list.

options.html: The reason shows politeness, which models are trained to reward
options.text: The reason shows politeness, which models are trained to reward
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The benefit has nothing to do with politeness. A reason lets the model apply the instruction to cases the instruction didn't list.

options.html: The reason is stored and reused in all of your later conversations
options.text: The reason is stored and reused in all of your later conversations
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A reason helps within the task at hand. It lets the model apply the instruction to cases the instruction didn't list.

options.html: The reason lets the model handle cases the instruction didn't list
options.text: The reason lets the model handle cases the instruction didn't list
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A model told that the text will be read aloud can avoid other things that can't be read aloud, even though the instruction named only one.

forms.stemHtml: You paste your organization's travel policy into a prompt and ask an AI assistant what the policy says about hotel costs. What does supplying the policy change about checking the answer?

options.html: You can check the answer against the policy you supplied
options.text: You can check the answer against the policy you supplied
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Supplied context narrows the checking to a comparison with your own document. The comparison still has to be done, because a model can misread what it's given.

options.html: You no longer need to check, since the model has the real policy
options.text: You no longer need to check, since the model has the real policy
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A model can skip a clause or state something the document doesn't say. Supplying the policy narrows the job to checking the answer against that policy.

options.html: You now have to check the answer against other travel policies
options.text: You now have to check the answer against other travel policies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Other organizations' policies aren't relevant to what yours says. Supplying the policy narrows the job to checking the answer against that policy.

options.html: You have more to check, since longer prompts cause more errors
options.text: You have more to check, since longer prompts cause more errors
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Relevant material makes the answer about your situation. Supplying the policy narrows the job to checking the answer against that policy.

forms.stemHtml: A teacher includes one past newsletter as an example in a prompt. The new newsletter comes back with the right tone and length, and it repeats the old newsletter's opening line and one of its dates. What happened?

options.html: Grounding, because the model worked from supplied material
options.text: Grounding, because the model worked from supplied material
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Grounding is working from material you supply for its facts. Here the model reused an example's particular details where only its pattern was wanted, which is over-copying.

options.html: Iteration, because the model improved on the earlier newsletter
options.text: Iteration, because the model improved on the earlier newsletter
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Iteration is improving a prompt in rounds. Here the model reused an example's particular details where only its pattern was wanted, which is over-copying.

options.html: Over-copying, because the model reused the example's details
options.text: Over-copying, because the model reused the example's details
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The model can't tell which features of an example you meant it to follow. Varying the examples and saying what to match both reduce the problem.

options.html: A missing goal, because the model didn't know the purpose
options.text: A missing goal, because the model didn't know the purpose
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The tone and length were right, so the purpose wasn't the problem. The model reused an example's particular details where only its pattern was wanted, which is over-copying.

forms.stemHtml: An output comes back generic and gets two of your facts wrong. Which of these are sound next steps? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Name exactly what is wrong with the output
options.text: Name exactly what is wrong with the output
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Diagnosis starts with naming the fault as exactly as you can.

options.html: Ask what the model wasn't told, and supply it
options.text: Ask what the model wasn't told, and supply it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Generic output with wrong facts points to missing context, so the revision adds the document or the facts.

options.html: Add words such as "excellent" and "detailed" to the prompt
options.text: Add words such as "excellent" and "detailed" to the prompt
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Adjectives add length without adding information the model lacked. The fix is to supply the missing facts.

options.html: Run the revised prompt again to see if the result holds
options.text: Run the revised prompt again to see if the result holds
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Output varies from run to run, so one better answer is weak evidence that the revision worked.

title: Prompts and context
